material_findings.evidence: The R35 runner used replace writes without a fresh-output guard or an exact R34 predecessor-registry guard. On the reviewed R38 tree, an accidental replay could overwrite the five R35 versioned outputs and replace the shared current registry with R35 before late validation, with no rollback or automatic failure receipt.
material_findings.comparison: R36, R37 and R38 promotion runners already require versioned outputs to be absent and the current registry to match the exact predecessor ID before writing.
material_findings.impact: Versioned-success immutability and the R38 source/object/index synchronization could be destroyed by an executable historical replay.
material_findings.required_fix: Before any write, require exact current registry R34 and all five R35 versioned outputs plus temporary outputs to be absent; add an R38-current zero-write rejection regression and preserve this failed audit as immutable evidence.

nonmaterial_findings.evidence: The top status still called the already completed full engineering gate the next step, while the appended R38 section recorded that gate as complete.
nonmaterial_findings.impact: A future operator could repeat an expensive gate or misread the current stage.
nonmaterial_findings.required_fix: Refresh the top status while retaining the historical record below.

verification_boundaries: The reviewer did not rerun pytest, compileall, pyflakes or a full chain under the strict read-only constraint.
The reviewer did not revisit external source pages and verified local captures, Git objects, private artifacts, hashes, lineage and authority only.
Remote GitHub transport was unavailable and the local branch was ahead four commits; this was not classified as a product failure.
